why: RULES['Heavy'] matches 24.16 word for word in rules/core-rules.md and Wahapedia core.html: "In your Shooting phase, each time an attack is made with a [HEAVY] weapon, add 1 to the hit roll if all of the following apply to the attacking unit: That unit is unengaged. / That unit was not set up on the battlefield this turn. / No model in that unit has moved more than 3" this turn." Its bold on 'hit roll' and 'unengaged' follows Wahapedia's <b>; the only difference is Wahapedia's underline on 'all', which is formatting. ruleFor strips the brackets and the anchored /^heavy$/i matches only 'HEAVY'/'[HEAVY]'/'Heavy' (a weapon keyword, the AdMech unit's rules chip, and the **[HEAVY]** in Protector Imperative). It does not match 'Heavy bolter', 'Heavy flamer', 'Heavy weapon' or 'SUPER-HEAVY WALKER' (that one goes to its own alias), and no faction alias or army rule is named 'heavy'.

For the two unplaced items it gives exactly New Recruit's line: "Hellfyre missile rack (x2) - Scarab Occult Terminators" becomes '2× … New Recruit lists them for the Scarab Occult Terminators, not which models carry them', and "Icon of Flame - Rubric Marines" becomes '1× … lists it for the Rubric Marines, not which model carries it'. The 1× matches the datasheet's "1 Rubric Marine can be equipped with 1 icon of flame". It finds a weapon by name, a multi-profile weapon by its group (the first profile's who/n), and an ability by name (check.js guarantees the name exists, so the {} fallback is not reached). It never names a models line: the Models and Bases rows only add a note (no base counted), and on the weapon row the carrier is 'which models: not said'. That is set before weaponJoins/useLine, and their 'name the one line' guesses skip items that already have a carrier or are on no gear line.

The new line `Object.entries(a.config || {}).map(([k, v]) => row(esc(k), f.armyRules.some(r => r.name === k) ? linkTo('rule', k, v) : esc(v)))` prints the label and value as given. For both Knights lists the data is { 'Code Chivalric':'Deed, Quality' }, word for word New Recruit's "• Code Chivalric: Deed, Quality". The value links to the army rule only on an exact name match (Imperial Knights armyRules has 'Code Chivalric'; showRule opens it) and is plain text otherwise. No other text is added, and the row is empty when an army has no config.
